content.title: About
content.content: Veal Marsala is a dish made from tender veal cutlets that are sautéed and then simmered in a sauce of dry Marsala wine, mushrooms, and onions. The dish has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor with aromatic notes of wine and earthy mushrooms.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Marsala wine is produced in Sicily and has been used in cooking for over a century.
Veal is considered more tender than beef because it contains less connective tissue.
Traditional recipes use button mushrooms, but other varieties can be substituted.
In the United States, Veal Marsala became popular in the mid‑20th century thanks to Italian restaurants.
The combination of Marsala wine and veal creates a natural balance of sweetness and acidity.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Veal provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with beef, veal generally contains less saturated fat, making it suitable for lower‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Veal is rich in B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The meat supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Antioxidants from wine
items.content: The Marsala‑based sauce adds polyphenols that have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef or veal.

items.title: Sodium content in sauce
items.content: Prepared sauce can be salty; people monitoring sodium intake should use it sparingly.

items.title: Alcohol in sauce
items.content: Although most alcohol evaporates during cooking, trace amounts may remain; consider this if avoiding alcohol.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Veal should be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella and other bacteria.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve Veal Marsala hot, typically with mashed potatoes, pasta, or rice. Garnish with fresh parsley or thyme for added flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When frozen, store for up to 2 months and thaw in the fridge before reheating.
